RC_STEPS|/plugR/short: A plug of FIX-20-T pressed into the dovetailed opening by hand and held until it hardens — after 1–2 minutes, with a noticeable warming.
RC_STEPS|/plugR/overview: Form plugs with the mortar and press them into the area where the water runs; hold by hand until the material has hardened. Hardening is preceded by a clearly noticeable warming. The plugged area is trowelled smooth immediately. {F20} solidifies even under water and swells against the concrete: chloride-free, with a strong bond and free of corrosion-promoting substances.
RC_STEPS|/plugR/points/0: consumption approx. 2 kg per litre of void
RC_STEPS|/plugR/points/1: compressive strength approx. 3 N/mm² after 1 hour, approx. 15 N/mm² after 24 hours, approx. 30 N/mm² after 28 days
RC_STEPS|/plugR/points/2: protect surfaces that are not to be treated from the effects of {F20}
RC_STEPS|/drainR/title: Set a drain under high water pressure
RC_STEPS|/drainR/short: A hose set in the strongest flow and fixed with FIX-20-T relieves the pressure; the hole is plugged after the hose is removed.
RC_STEPS|/drainR/overview: If the water pressure is high, a drain is installed using water hoses or pipes: the water pressure is minimised, which makes tamping easier. A depression is chiselled out in the area of the strongest water flow, the hose or pipe is fixed in place with {F20} mortar and the surrounding leak is plugged. After drying the hose is removed and the hole is plugged with mortar as described.
RC_STEPS|/drainR/points/0: the drain runs while the joint around it is plugged with {F20}
RC_STEPS|/drainR/points/1: remove the hose or pipe after drying; plug the hose hole with a {F20} plug pressed in by hand
RC_STEPS|/drainR/points/2: the plugged areas are afterwards made good with {IM} and coated with {IC}
RC_STEPS|/mixIM/short: 3.75–4.25 l of water per 25 kg, approx. 3 minutes to a homogeneous, lump-free filler consistency; pot life approx. 30 minutes.
RC_STEPS|/mixIM/overview: Add water (3.75–4.25 l per 25 kg) to a clean mixing bucket and mix with 25 kg of the powder component to produce a homogeneous, lump-free mass of filler consistency. Stirrer approx. 500–700 rpm with a suitable mixing paddle.
RC_STEPS|/mixIM/points/0: mixing time approx. 3 minutes; pot life approx. 30 minutes at approx. 5–30 °C
RC_STEPS|/mixIM/points/1: grain size < 1 mm; up to 10 mm per application step
RC_STEPS|/mixIM/points/2: rinse tools with water immediately after use
RC_STEPS|/fillR/title: Fill the cracks and holes with ASOCRET-IM
RC_STEPS|/fillR/short: Edges screened with AQUAFIN-IC, the chased crack filled flush with ASOCRET-IM wet in wet, up to 10 mm per step.
RC_STEPS|/fillR/overview: Structural cracks prised open to approx. 20 mm width and 25 mm depth: the edges are screened with {IC} and sealed wet in wet with {IM} flush with the surface. {IM} can be applied with a layer thickness of up to 10 mm per application step. The mortar is capillary active and supports the self-repair of the concrete; it must be protected against rapid water removal.
RC_STEPS|/fillR/points/0: consumption approx. 1.3 kg per metre of U-shaped crack (20 × 25 mm); approx. 1.7 kg/m² per mm of layer
RC_STEPS|/fillR/points/1: after approx. 1–3 hours the mortar is reworked with {IC}; if this is not possible during this period, the surface is roughened after total hardening and then coated
RC_STEPS|/fillR/points/2: faulty areas and voids are repaired with {F20} or alternatively {IM}; larger voids with the ASOCRET-BIS system
RC_STEPS|/fillR/points/3: do not use on frozen substrates; the reaction with the free lime of the concrete can result in slight efflorescence — not a defect, brushed off
RC_STEPS|/coveR/short: ASOCRET-IM on a screen of AQUAFIN-IC, wet in wet, edge height approx. 4 cm, rounded; AQUAFIN-IC over it after 1–3 hours.
RC_STEPS|/coveR/overview: The substrate at the wall–floor joint is screened with {IC}; the {IM} is then applied wet in wet with an edge height of approx. 4 cm in a rounded form. After approx. 1–3 hours the fillet is reworked with {IC}. If this is not possible during this period, the surface is roughened after total hardening and then coated.
RC_STEPS|/coveR/points/0: consumption approx. 1.3 kg per metre (edge height 38 mm)
RC_STEPS|/coveR/points/1: pointing trowel; the fillet is protected against rapid water removal
RC_STEPS|/coveR/points/2: the fillet forms part of the crystalline system: {IM} is capillary active with increased crack healing
RC_STEPS|/mixIC/short: 6.75–8 l of water per 25 kg, stirred vigorously for approx. 3 minutes, matured, mixed again; pot life approx. 60 minutes.
RC_STEPS|/mixIC/overview: Depending on the desired consistency, pour 6.75–8 l of water per 25 kg into a clean mixing bucket and add enough powder while stirring vigorously until the mortar is homogeneous and clump-free (approx. 27–32 % water). After a maturing time of approx. 3–5 minutes mix again.
RC_STEPS|/mixIC/points/0: stirrer approx. 500–700 rpm with a suitable mixing paddle
RC_STEPS|/mixIC/points/1: pot life approx. 60 minutes at a substrate and application temperature of approx. 5–30 °C
RC_STEPS|/mixIC/points/3: for spraying see Technical Information No. 43
RC_STEPS|/coatR1/short: AQUAFIN-IC brushed evenly into the matt damp concrete with the wide brush or broom, or sprayed, free of pores.
RC_STEPS|/coatR1/overview: The surfaces are dampened once more with clean water so that they are matt damp without puddles; {IC} is applied in a minimum of two application steps, ensuring it is free of pores, brushed evenly and worked into the substrate meticulously. Consumption approx. 1 kg per m² and mm.
RC_STEPS|/coatR1/points/0: wide brush, roofer’s broom or spray equipment; machine application after Technical Information No. 43
RC_STEPS|/coatR1/points/1: brush the slurry into the chased and filled details and over the fresh fillet as well (after 1–3 hours)
RC_STEPS|/coatR1/points/2: protect surfaces that are not to be treated from the effects of {IC}
RC_STEPS|/coatR2/title: Apply the second coat wet in sticky
RC_STEPS|/coatR2/short: The second coat while the first is still sticky and has not dried out; to the material rate of the water load.
RC_STEPS|/coatR2/overview: Apply the second layer while the first layer is still sticky and has not yet dried out: drying of the first layer must be avoided. The total rate follows the water load: 0.75 kg/m² in one layer for soil moisture and non-accumulating seepage water; 1.2 kg/m² in two layers for non-pressurised water; 1.5 kg/m² in two layers for accumulated water.
RC_STEPS|/coatR2/points/0: increased material consumption for uneven surfaces is excluded from these rates
RC_STEPS|/coatR2/points/1: foot traffic after approx. 5 hours; withstands pressurised water after ≥ 7 days
RC_STEPS|/coatR2/points/2: movement and connecting joints: ASO-Dichtband system components in accordance with their data sheets
RC_STEPS|/cureR/short: Protected from sun, wind, rain and frost for ≥ 24 hours; kept damp for ≥ 3 days from the day after application — jute sheets, water mist.
RC_STEPS|/cureR/overview: The fresh coating is protected against weathering influences for ≥ 24 hours. The waterproofing layer must be kept damp for ≥ 3 days: the initial dampening takes place one day after application and is repeated at set intervals; in case of strong solar radiation or wind, water-soaked jute sheets are recommended. The material cures very well in areas with high humidity; in relatively dry areas the coating is kept damp for at least 3 days.
RC_STEPS|/cureR/points/0: in poorly ventilated rooms and deep pits adequate ventilation is provided for 24 hours
RC_STEPS|/cureR/points/1: in rooms with high humidity or insufficient ventilation (e.g. water containers) dropping below the dew point can occur on the surface: avoid it with condensation dryers — direct heating or uncontrolled blowing of warm air is not permitted
RC_STEPS|/cureR/points/2: in service water tanks at approx. +10 to +15 °C the coating is kept damp at a constant relative humidity > 80 % and protected against drying; 7 days are generally sufficient for complete hydration
RC_STEPS|/cureR/points/3: backfilling of a building pit can take place 3 days after coating
RC_STEPS|/fillR2/short: Filling after 3 days; drinking water tanks rinsed thoroughly first; pressurised water after ≥ 7 days; the slurry stays active.
RC_STEPS|/fillR2/overview: Filling of containers is possible after 3 days. Drinking water tanks are rinsed out thoroughly with drinking water before filling. {IC} withstands pressurised water after ≥ 7 days and may require at least one month to achieve its maximum sealing characteristics, depending on temperature, humidity, type of cement and concrete composition. When properly applied, it is permanently active.
RC_STEPS|/fillR2/points/0: the reaction with the free lime in the concrete can result in slight efflorescence: not a defect, removed with a broom
RC_STEPS|/fillR2/points/1: a different colouring depends on the different moisture content in the concrete
RC_STEPS|/fillR2/points/2: cracks that develop later, up to 0.4 mm, are sealed by renewed crystal growth
RC_STEPS|/dryR/short: The pit stays dry; the crystals keep growing wherever water arrives — permanently active.
RC_STEPS|/dryR/overview: {IC} withstands pressurised water after ≥ 7 days; the maximum sealing effect can take up to one month. The coating is vapour permeable and permanently active: cracks up to 0.4 mm that develop later are sealed again. Efflorescence from the free lime of the concrete is brushed off.
RC_STEPS|/dryR/points/0: negative pressing water up to 1.5 bar
RC_STEPS|/dryR/points/1: the pit stays ventilated until the coating has cured; no direct heating
RC_STEPS|/dryR/points/2: the coating cannot be overcoated with tiles, plaster, bonded screeds or paint
RC_STEPS|/crystalR/title: How the crystals seal the concrete
RC_STEPS|/crystalR/short: Active ingredients penetrate the capillaries with the water, react with moisture and free lime and fill the smallest pores and cracks with crystals.
RC_STEPS|/crystalR/overview: Once applied to the concrete surface, the active ingredients from the waterproofing material penetrate inside the building component and cause a brisk crystal growth. The smallest pores and cracks become filled with crystals and impermeable to capillary water. “Foe becomes friend”: water penetrating the component behaves as a transport medium for the active ingredients and takes them deep into the substrate.
RC_STEPS|/crystalR/points/0: the coating remains permanently active and seals cracks of up to 0.4 mm that develop later
RC_STEPS|/crystalR/points/1: vapour permeable (class I), carbonation reducing, chloride-free
RC_STEPS|/crystalR/points/2: the same mechanism in the repair mortar {IM} (capillary active, increased crack healing) and the plugging mortar {F20} (crystalline sealing effect)
RC_STEPS|/aggR/short: Hardness < 30 mg CaO per litre or aggressive water: a water analysis is always required; degree of attack after EN 1992-1-1.
RC_STEPS|/aggR/overview: If {IC} is applied in containers or in case of water loading with aggressive or soft water featuring a hardness < 30 mg CaO per litre, a water analysis is always required. The degree of attack is evaluated in accordance with EN 1992-1-1 (Eurocode 2).
RC_STEPS|/aggR/points/0: sewage, sludge and septic tanks are among the fields of application of {IC}
RC_STEPS|/aggR/points/1: in containers dropping below the dew point is avoided with condensation dryers
RC_STEPS|/aggR/points/2: the coating cannot be overcoated with tiles, plaster, bonded screeds or paint
RC_STEPS|/cleanR/title: Clean the tools, store the material
RC_STEPS|/cleanR/short: Tools rinsed with water immediately after use; bags and pails stored cool and dry.
RC_STEPS|/cleanR/overview: Tools are rinsed with water immediately after use. {IC} is stored cool and dry for min. 12 months in the original container, {IM} cool, dry and protected from sunlight for min. 18 months, {F20} likewise for min. 12 months. Opened containers are used promptly. Observe the applicable safety data sheets.
RC_STEPS|/cleanR/points/0: {IM} and {IC} cannot be admixed as an additive to concrete or plaster
RC_STEPS|/cleanR/points/1: surfaces that are not to be treated are protected from the effects of the mortars
RC_STEPS|/cleanR/points/2: observe the applicable safety data sheets
RCS_T|/rctank/name: Drinking and service water tank, from the inside
RCS_T|/rctank/problem: A concrete tank holds water permanently: a water-bearing crack and a leaking construction joint let it through, lime leaches out along them, the concrete carbonates. The tank has to be tight, and — for drinking water — the coating must be suitable for it.
RCS_T|/rctank/solution: The tank is drained and jetted; static cracks over 0.4 mm and the joint are chased 20 × 25 mm, screened with {IC} and filled flush with {IM}; the coved fillet of approx. 4 cm follows wet in wet. Two coats of {IC} — 1.5 kg/m² for accumulated water — are brushed into the matt damp concrete and kept damp for 3 days; the tank is rinsed and filled after 3 days. Tested for drinking water (DVGW W 270 / W 347), 14 bar (CRD-C 48-92), permanently active.
RCS_T|/rcwall/name: Basement wall from the inside, negative pressing water
RCS_T|/rcwall/problem: Ground water presses through a construction joint of an in-situ concrete basement wall: the joint leaks, lime leaches out, at its foot the water runs in. The outside cannot be dug up, so the waterproofing has to hold the pressure from the negative side.
RCS_T|/rcwall/solution: The running water is stopped with a plug of {F20} pressed into the dovetailed opening; the joint and the cracks are chased 20 × 25 mm and filled with {IM} on a screen of {IC}, the coved fillet of approx. 4 cm at the floor; then two coats of {IC} (1.5 kg/m²) brushed into the matt damp concrete — watertight against negative pressing water up to 1.5 bar, the crystals growing into the capillaries. Kept damp ≥ 3 days, ventilated, no condensation.
RCS_T|/rcpit/name: Lift pit with active water ingress
RCS_T|/rcpit/problem: The pit of a lift shaft lies below the ground water level: water enters under pressure at the wall–floor joint and through an old anchor hole, stands in the pit and cannot be pumped away for good. Access only from the inside, in a confined and poorly ventilated space.
RCS_T|/rcpit/solution: A drain hose set into a chiselled depression at the strongest flow and fixed with {F20} relieves the pressure while the joint is plugged with {F20}; after drying the hose is removed and its hole plugged. The coved fillet of {IM} of approx. 4 cm on a screen of {IC}, then two coats of {IC} over walls and floor (1.5 kg/m²). Kept damp ≥ 3 days, the pit ventilated for 24 hours — the pit stays dry, the coating stays active.
RCS_T|/rcsew/name: Sewage and sludge tank, aggressive water
RCS_T|/rcsew/problem: Sewage, sludge and septic tanks hold aggressive, often soft water: sludge and biofilm cover the concrete, cracks and the inlet leak, the humid, poorly ventilated container condenses. The concrete must be sealed against the water and the water kept away from the concrete.
RCS_T|/rcsew/solution: A water analysis first (hardness < 30 mg CaO per litre; degree of attack after EN 1992-1-1). Sludge and biofilm are jetted off; cracks are chased and filled with {IM}, larger voids re-profiled with the ASOCRET-BIS system; then two coats of {IC} (1.5 kg/m²) into the matt damp concrete — chloride-free, carbonation reducing, vapour permeable. Condensation is avoided with dryers, the coating is kept damp ≥ 3 days at a relative humidity > 80 %; filling after 3 days.
RCS_T|/layers/plugL/1: {F20} pressed by hand into the dovetailed opening until it hardens — after 1–2 minutes, even under running water; trowelled smooth
RCS_T|/layers/plugL/3: approx. 2 kg per litre of void
